en: The Apadāna of the Elder Saparivāriya Chapter on the Parasols (Chattavagga), Number 4 I was a king named Mahāpabbata, possessing great power and majesty. At that time, the Buddha Kassapa appeared in the world. Having heard of the Teacher’s arrival, I went forth into homelessness. I took up the three robes and the alms-bowl, and I practiced the holy life. For twenty thousand years I dwelt in the forest, practicing meditation and striving for the goal. Then, having attained the fruit of Arhatship, I passed away from that existence. By the power of that wholesome deed, I was reborn in heaven. After enjoying celestial bliss for sixty thousand aeons, I was born here in the human world. In this very city of Bārāṇasī, I became a king; my name was Mahāpabbata, and I possessed great power and majesty. At that time, the Buddha Gotama appeared in the world. “The Victor named Padumuttara,
the eldest in the world, the bull among men,
having blazed like a mass of fire— ”
The Perfectly Enlightened One has attained final nibbāna.
And when the Great Hero had attained nibbāna,
his stupa became widespread.
Even from afar they pay homage to the most excellent shrine of the relics;
with a confident mind and a joyful heart, they do so.
I made a sandalwood railing;
at that time, the trunk of the stupa appeared, worthy of a stupa.
While being reborn in existence,
whether as a deity or as a human,
I do not perceive even a slight deficiency in myself.
This is the fruit of past karma.
Fifteen hundred eons ago, there were eight people here.
All those named Samatta were wheel-turning monarchs of great power.
The four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā) [are theirs].
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder, together with his retinue, speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Saparivāriya is the fourth.
